label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Hello Tolu. I'm Amaka, I'm in Biology 100L now, and I wanted Medicine. I'm writing this because I'd have wanted someone to be straight with me when I was where you are.

I scored 251 in JAMB 2025. I applied for Medicine and Surgery and got Biology at a federal university here in Lagos. The day I saw it on the portal, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't eat. My mum had already been telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for like two months, and I had to beg her to stop. So I understand why you've been crying since afternoon. It's a real loss, and you're allowed to feel it before you decide anything.

Now the transfer part, because that's what you need.

Yes, transfer to Medicine from Biology is possible in some schools. Our level adviser told us the basic conditions: you need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5 after 100L, and there must be space. She also said that last year about 6 people were moved into MBBS from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 people applied. So the odds are not good, and anyone who tells you it's automatic is wrong. Kingsley saying it's a myth is also wrong, because it happens. But favour saying just read hard is too simple. Reading hard matters, but the space is the thing you don't control.

Also, the CGPA is not the only thing. Medicine cut-offs in JAMB and post-UTME are part of it too, and you need to check your school's own cut-offs and your post-UTME score against them. Your 268 alone doesn't tell anyone whether you're eligible. I don't know your school's rules, and I'm not going to guess them for you.

I'm being honest about my own position. My CGPA after first semester is 4.31. That's not 4.5, so I'm not there yet. I'm still trying. Some people in my set are doing better than me and some are doing worse. I don't know yet if I'll make it, and I won't pretend I do.

What I can tell you is what 100L is actually like. The courses are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101, and GST. Physics and maths are the ones that deal with people, so if you're not comfortable with those, take that seriously and get help early. Lab coat cost me 6,500 naira, dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual was extra. So budget for that before you start.

The thing nobody told me is that I actually like it. In our first BIO practical we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted. I was fine, and that day I realised I actually enjoy this thing. I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected. I didn't expect that. Biology is not a bad course. It's not a consolation prize either, but it's also not the same as Medicine, and I won't tell you it is.

Let me also be fair about the rewrite side. Rewriting is not wrong if you're truly ready. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she's still at home. I'm not saying that to scare you. I'm saying staying home is not as easy as people make it sound. You watch your mates go to school, you deal with people asking what's happening, and the pressure builds. If you rewrite, do it because you're ready to work again and you're clear about what you want, not just because you're hurt right now.

Which brings me to the questions you need to ask yourself. Do you want Medicine, or do you want to be a doctor because of what it will mean to your parents and people at church? Those are not the same. Be honest with yourself about that before you decide anything. Also, your acceptance deadline is in two weeks, so don't let the decision get rushed. If you reject it, you're not sure of getting another chance right away. If you accept, you can still look at transfer and rewriting later.

Please don't just trust forum people, including me. Go to your faculty or department and ask the exact transfer rules for your own school. Ask what the CGPA requirement is, how many spaces there are, what the Medicine cut-offs are, and how the post-UTME is weighted. Write the answers down. Those are the facts you need, not our gist.

Whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world. People change courses, people transfer, people rewrite and still become doctors, and people find they like a course they didn't pick. You don't have to know your whole future tonight. Eat something, talk to someone who loves you, and then go find out the facts.

If you want to ask me anything specific about 100L, the practicals, or how the first semester went, ask here. I'll answer honestly.
